target_rule.rule: median row count of the parent's Index-presentation train-split families (a training-draw quantity; no eval rate or shape)

esci_relevance.export: first occurrence per example_id; US locale; product_id and normalised query not in any Index ESCI row; state <= 4500 chars; first 9000 by sha256(seed|example_id) (seed 20261009); natural label rates
esci_relevance.n_generated_rule: ceil(1.6 * target), trimmed to the target after the checks
esci_relevance.rule: uniform over eligible train pairs (sha256 order); natural train label rates; half Index presentation (ids E/S/C/I, question 'answer'), half schema view

index_fingerprint_item_tier.rule: data.dedup.Fingerprint (production index-fp-v3, all Index rows) on the row's ITEM-tier texts; any matcher (exact / ngram13 / minhash / edit / contain) drops the row, as the parent builds

nli4ct_trial.rule: train statements whose primary and secondary trial are in no Index NLI4CT row (all 5,500 test statements' trial_ids); natural train label rate; views per item = 2 when 2 x eligible <= target (view 0 Index presentation, view 1 schema view with the statement in state), else 1; the P3 checker keeps one Index-presentation row per trial section (state + options text repeats across statements)
nli4ct_trial.n_target_rule: min(T, views x eligible items): train availability caps the family

index_fingerprint_item_tier.rule: data.dedup.Fingerprint (production index-fp-v3, all Index rows) on the row's ITEM-tier texts; any matcher (exact / ngram13 / minhash / edit / contain) drops the row, as the parent builds

phish_email.rule: uniform over the eligible union (sha256 order): natural corpus rate; questions verdict / is_phishing / verdict_alt_click from the corpus label; half Index presentation, half schema view
